categories.label: Retail
categories.words: Up to ₹2 lakh. Most people apply here.
categories.odds_words: About 1 in 3 applicants gets one lot (an estimate, from 2.7x bids).
categories.note: Applying for more lots doesn't raise your chance: when retail is oversubscribed, each winner gets one lot.

categories.label: Small HNI (sHNI)
categories.words: More than ₹2 lakh, up to ₹10 lakh.
categories.odds_words: About 1 in 10 applicants gets the smallest application (an estimate, from 10.2x bids).

categories.label: Big HNI (bHNI)
categories.odds_words: About 1 in 16 applicants gets the smallest application (an estimate, from 15.9x bids).

odds_note: From the final bids, after bidding closed.

verdicts.label: Wait, and think about buying after it lists
verdicts.track_record: A weak predictor of 1-year returns, about a coin flip: past IPOs with this verdict beat the Nifty 50 over 1 year 50% of the time (tested on 22 IPOs from 2024–25). Use it to understand the business, not to pick winners.

exits.title: Your listing-day rule
steps: Before Wed 28 Oct: decide your rule now, while you're calm, and write it in your journal.
On Wed 28 Oct, the shares start trading at 10 AM. Don't buy more on the first day's excitement.
If it opens above ₹1,119: you applied for a listing gain, so sell on listing day. Waiting for more turns a plan into a hope.
If it opens below ₹1,119: sell if it is more than 10% below your price, rather than holding on to wait for it to come back.

disclaimer: A learning aid worked out by fixed rules, not advice. Only apply with money you won't need soon, and decide for yourself.
